tests: Suppress PhanAbstractStaticMethodCallInStatic/…Trait

In preparation for enabling Phan on some test files (I2ea263e83c32).

Phan hates this pattern:

class/trait A {
abstract public static method foo();
public static method bar() {
static::foo();
}
}

…because it is possible to call A::bar() directly from other code,
which would call the abstract method A::foo(), which would cause
a runtime error.

Usually you'd avoid it by designing your interface to not use static
methods, which make all kinds of things awkward. However, it is
impossible to avoid when the abstract method is used by a PHPUnit test
provider, which must be public static methods. So just suppress the
PhanAbstractStaticMethodCallInStatic/PhanAbstractStaticMethodCallInTrait
warnings in these tests. I'm not really sure how much value this issue
has in general, anyway.

FileRepo: Switch getDescriptionShortUrl from curid to Special:Redirect

Prefer Special:Redirect (which redirects to canonical) over `?curid=`:
* Let search engines follow and carry pagerank (avoid robots.txt disallow)
* Faster response to user by leveraging CDN cache
* Reduce CDN cache misses

Canonical (for comparison)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rain_Quail_in_Bhigwan_August_2025_by_Tisha_Mukherjee_13.jpg

Before this patch (MediaWiki default)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=172562139

After this patch (MediaWiki default)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/page/172562139

Proposed for WMF (later patch)
https://commons.wikimedia.org/entity/M172562139

tests: Add `@extends` to many test traits

This allows Phan to assume the existence of methods, properties etc.
provided by the named class (or trait), and documents that the traits
should be used only with the named class (or trait).

Otherwise we would have to list each individually using
`@method`/`@property` etc. annotations or abstract methods.

I'm only adding these annotations, mostly just guessing which is
right and not really checking, so they may be a bit wrong:
@extends \PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase

@extends \MediaWikiIntegrationTestCase
@extends \MediaWikiTestCaseTrait

In case of MediaWikiTestCaseTrait, this also requires suppressing
PhanAccessWrongInheritanceCategory, since you're not supposed to
extend traits (only use them).

Phan probably should have a more specific annotation for
this use case, something like `@phpstan-require-extends`
and `@psalm-require-extends`, but currently it doesn't.

Also add some commonly used abstract methods on MediaWikiTestCaseTrait
(which are identical between MediaWiki unit and integration tests).

old_description:
Add deferred blocks

Add an option to Special:Block (both the legacy and the Codex form)
and to action=block for placing a deferred block. A deferred block is
not enforced, and is hidden from the blocked user, until the user
attempts an action that the block prevents. That action is blocked,
and the block materializes: it becomes a normal block, and is logged
in the block log by the sysop who placed it, with its absolute expiry.
The expiry counts from when the block was placed, so a deferred block
that is never triggered just expires.

Storage:
* Deferred blocks are stored as normal rows in the block table, with

the rest route configuration. This makes the hybrid action API module
aware that it's running in "REST mode", and allows it to react to
specifics of the route declaration.

Information about the REST route is injected into the API module as an
ApiRestHelperContext object. GenericActionHandler and GenericListHandler
now ensure that the context always gets injected before the module
object is used.

NOTE: This changes the ApiRestHybrid interface, which is marked @stable
in 1.47. Needs a backport!

old_description:
Recover page when page_latest is 0 or unpopulated

When a page row has page_latest set to 0, MessageCache fails to load system messages like MediaWiki:Sidebar, viewing the page renders an unhandled error box, and editing triggers a false edit conflict loop.

Look up the latest revision from the revision table when page_latest is 0 across RevisionStore and WikiPage, delegate missing text in Article to showMissingArticle(), and allow PageUpdater to heal corrupted page rows on save.
new_description:
Recover page when page_latest is 0 or unpopulated

When a page exists in the page table with page_id > 0 but page_latest is 0
or not populated (e.g. from an interrupted create, restore, or corrupt row):
- RevisionLookup::getKnownLatestRevision() returned false, causing MessageCache
to fail loading system messages like MediaWiki:Sidebar and making the sidebar
disappear across all pages of the wiki.
- Article::generateContentOutput() treated the missing revision as a fatal error
displaying an 'Error' box with 'noarticletext' instead of calling
showMissingArticle().
- Saving an edit to the page failed because PageUpdater::doCreate() aborted with
'edit-already-exists' when attempting to insert the existing page row.

Fix this by:
1. RevisionStore: in getKnownLatestRevision(), if rev_id could not be found
from page_latest, query the latest rev_id from the revision table as a fallback.
2. Article: in generateContentOutput(), if the fetch error has the message
'noarticletext', delegate to showMissingArticle() instead of showViewError().
3. PageUpdater: in doCreate(), if page insertion indicates the row already exists
and page_latest is 0, reuse the existing page ID to attach the revision and
update page_latest, healing the page row.

ParserOutputAccess: Clear stale parser cache metadata after PoolCounter wait

Since 67557ba1899 (T277829), ParserCache::getMetadata() keeps whatever
it read from the persistent cache in its in-process cache, including
entries that are outdated for the page and so are a miss.

That breaks PoolCounter stampede protection. A request that misses
because of an edit has already read the metadata for the previous
revision. It waits for the lock, and when the holder has saved output
for the new revision, doCachedWork() looks it up again, finds the old
metadata in the in-process cache, and misses. PoolCounterWork then
calls execute( true ), which renders the page again and saves it
again. Each waiter does this in turn.

Add ParserCache::clearLocalCache(), and call it in doCachedWork()
before the lookup, so that it reads what the other process saved.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5
Follows-Up: I4b2d925ec1d27223d6b135e485de53be24a099d0
new_description:
ParserOutputAccess: Clear stale parser cache metadata after PoolCounter wait

Since 67557ba1899 (T277829), ParserCache::getMetadata() keeps whatever
it read from the persistent cache in its in-process cache, including
entries that are outdated for the page and so are a miss.

That breaks PoolCounter stampede protection. A request that misses
because of an edit has already read the metadata for the previous
revision. It waits for the lock, and when the holder has saved output
for the new revision, doCachedWork() looks it up again, finds the old
metadata in the in-process cache, and misses. PoolCounterWork then
calls execute( true ), which renders the page again and saves it
again. Each waiter does this in turn.

The stale fallback has the same problem on the postproc path. When
there is no postproc output, getFallbackOutputForLatest() reads the
outdated base entry with getDirty(), which keeps it in the in-process
cache. If the fallback is declined and the request then gets the lock,
renderRevision() misses the base output that the holder saved, and
parses the page again.

Add ParserCache::clearLocalCache(), and call it in doCachedWork()
before the lookup, and in getFallbackOutputForLatest() after reading
the base entry, so that later lookups read what the other process
saved.

metadataProcCache. If the stale/dirty output is then rejected

already stored updated canonical content in the cache.

the lookup and in getFallbackOutputForLatest() after reading the
canonical output. This ensures that lookups on both of these paths
read what the other process saved from the persistent cache, not the
potentially-outdated contents of their in-process cache.

old_description:
RawAction: Use CDN maxage, remove wgForcedRawSMaxage, ignore maxage/smaxage

The ignoring of the 'maxage' and 'smaxage' parameters is not considered
a breaking change since we still respond with the same content, and
under HTTP semantics caching can and does change for various reasons
already. For example, at WMF these were generally overridden at the
edge, and for plain MW installs, numerous protections in MW also at
differemt times override these.

The bulk of action=raw is canonical CSS/JS urls for public content.

== Before ==

These were previously emitted with "Cache-Control: public" and
s-maxage of 5 minutes, and maxage of 31 days. At WMF, this is then
read by ATS/Varnish cache as instruction to cache with TTL of 5min,
and to the end-user the header is swapped out with "private,
must-revalidate, max-age=0", even for logged-in users, since it the
URLs don't match exemptions we have in place for '/static' or
'/w/load.php', and the origin does have session cookies.

== After ==

Change to "Cache-Control: public, must-revalidate" and s-maxage of
31 days, and max-age of 5min.

== client max-age ==

I don't know why we used the "CDN" value to set "client" max-age.
That's confusing and looks like a mistake, and is currently ignored
at WMF, as the edge strips that header out. I suspect this was an
accidental default never used in practice, as internal use of
action=raw for the special '-' title always set its own smaxage. We
probably did want browsers to blindly cache the "main" css/js bundle
as long as possible. Anyhow, that special endpoint was removed in
2011, and the main source of these URLs is now legacy.js importScript,
which doesn't use these params, and I've generally encouraged and
helped the community to remove these from existing scripts - to allow
CDN caching and purging to work, which requires absence of these query
parameters.

== s-maxage ==
This was previously shortened to 5min. Again, that's from when we
used the special '-' title, rather than for regular wiki content.
Kind of like RL's startup module, I guess we wanted changes to the
software frontend to roll out quickly across prod. But, this endpoint
no longer exists, and action=raw now supports wiki content only, which
we purge on edit, so it's okay to let the CDN cache these for longer,
same as articles (defaults to 31 days, 14 days at WMF).

Note that RawAction used OutputPage::checkLastModified for 304
responses, which already uses wgCdnMaxAge to deny renewal of caches
from before (now - wgCdnMaxAge). This is mainly for page views to
ensure no untracked variance (e.g. skin layout, site config etc.) is
served older than wgCdnMaxAge, even if the page itself was not
"modified". This shoudln't matter for action=raw, though.
new_description:
RawAction: Enable full CDN caching for canonical CSS/JSON/JS URLs

== What ==

* For the bulk of action=raw URLs, increase CDN caching from 5 min
($wgForcedRawSMaxage) to 14 days ($wgCdnMaxAge, 14 days at WMF).

This matches how we cache pageviews.

* Replace broken "maxage" blind browser caching and set it to 5 min.

* Remove (partially broken) "smaxage" and "maxage" params.

* Remove $wgForcedRawSMaxage, obsoleted by $wgCdnMaxAge, and
was internal only to RawAction. Never read or set anywhere.

== Why ==

* Reduce server load by increasing CDN caching.
The canonical CSS/JSON/JS URLs are already purged on edit, making
this an easy win-win (for infra load, for users, and for devs).

* Remove self-defeating maxage/smaxage. It is strictly worse to set
this parameter. After the above change, by omitting the param, you
get longer caching, yet also enjoy timely purges.

* Remove confusing and broken code.

This code was (attempting to) set maxage to $wgCdnMaxAge, which is
confusing because that's meant to control CDN caching (s-maxage)
instead of browser caching (max-age).s

It is broken in production because of the way our CDN strips
"s-maxage" from the Cache-Control header on /w/index.php
responses. The CDN does this (since forever) because we don't want
external proxies or browsers to blindy cache article content in a
way we can't invalidate. MediaWiki pageviews set
"s-maxage=$wgCdnMaxAge, max-age=0" and Varnish replaces this with
"s-maxage=0, max-age=0" [1] [2]. But when something other than a
pageview wants browsing caching (like action=raw), it gets lost.

* Improve page load time for both logged-out users and logged-in
users by allowing limited browser-side caching. I propose 5min,
which matches the well-known 5min cadance of ResourceLoader,
as a way to be least surprising. It has been established since
2011 that edits to CSS/JS/JSON are live everywhere within 5 min,
which now applies to action=raw as wel.

This won't actually work until we fix Varnish as well.

== History ==

* 2007 (SVN r27456) Introduce $wgForcedRawSMaxage
* 2015 (I7f3b67780) RawAction clean up

[2] https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/c/operations/puppet/+/65541

== What ==

* For the bulk of action=raw URLs, increase CDN caching from 5 min
($wgForcedRawSMaxage) to 14 days ($wgCdnMaxAge, 14 days at WMF).

This matches how we cache pageviews.

* Replace broken "maxage" blind browser caching and set it to 5 min.

* Reduce server load by increasing CDN caching.
The canonical CSS/JSON/JS URLs are already purged on edit, making
this an easy win-win (for infra load, for users, and for devs).

* Remove self-defeating maxage/smaxage. It is strictly worse to set
this parameter. After the above change, by omitting the param, you
get longer caching, yet also enjoy timely purges.

* Remove confusing and broken code.

This code was (attempting to) set maxage to $wgCdnMaxAge, which is
confusing because that's meant to control CDN caching (s-maxage)
instead of browser caching (max-age).

It is broken in production because of the way our CDN strips
"s-maxage" from the Cache-Control header on /w/index.php
responses. The CDN does this (since forever) because we don't want
external proxies or browsers to blindy cache article content in a
way we can't invalidate. MediaWiki pageviews set

"s-maxage=0, max-age=0" [1] [2]. But when something other than a

which matches the well-known 5min cadance of ResourceLoader,
as a way to be least surprising. It has been established since
2011 that edits to CSS/JS/JSON are live everywhere within 5 min,
which now applies to action=raw as wel.

phpunit: output to stdout and don't start a buffer

Previously, we would print output to stderr and start an output buffer
to avoid "headers already sent" warnings due to tests calling
`header()`. However, both options complicate our PHPUnit config and have
shown to be poorly supported by other tools (for example, the
slow-test-detector, the infection framework, and paratest). So, drop
these options from the PHPUnit config, and instead:

- For widely-used code that outputs headers (such as
ContentSecurityPolicy), don't send headers in tests. If a test will
ever need to exercise those headers, we could add a setter and a flag
to skip this check, but for now that is not needed.
- For code that is self-contained but can be invoked by unrelated tests
(such as special pages, executed by SpecialPageFatalTest), throw
exceptions instead of emitting HTTP headers while in tests, and adjust
expectations accordingly.
- For tests that actually exercise headers, or where disabling the
header is not practical, tell PHPUnit to run the test in a separate
process. We also disable global state preservation, as some of our
(config) globals contain closures that cannot be serialized, and they
would be re-set by the bootstrap in the child process anyway.

old_description:
ParserCache: Don't let a stale in-process entry hide a newer one

Since 67557ba1899 (T277829), getMetadata() keeps whatever it read from
the persistent cache in the in-process cache, including entries that
are outdated or expired for the page, and so are a miss. Later lookups
in the same process use that entry and never look at the persistent
cache again.

That breaks PoolCounter stampede protection in ParserOutputAccess. A
request that misses because of an edit waits for the lock, and when
the holder has saved output for the new revision, doCachedWork() looks
it up again. It finds the old entry in the in-process cache, misses,
and calls execute( true ), which renders the page again and saves it
again. Each waiter does this in turn.

Make a miss based on the in-process entry never final: if that entry
would be rejected for the given staleness constraint, read the
persistent cache. Lookups that accept the entry, such as getDirty() or
getMetadata() with the default constraint, still use the in-process
cache, so the duplicate reads of T277829 stay fixed in the common case.
Callers do not need to clear anything.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

Language: Deprecate passing null to the case-conversion methods

ucfirst(), lcfirst(), uc(), lc(), ucwords(), ucwordbreaks() and caseFold()
all document `@param string` but enforce nothing, so a null from a caller
reaches PHP's internal functions and produces a diagnostic that points at
Language.php rather than at whoever passed the null.

ucfirst( null ) currently emits three of them:

Warning: Trying to access array offset on null
Deprecated: ord(): Passing null to parameter #1 ($character) of type
string is deprecated
Deprecated: ord(): Providing an empty string is deprecated

T410920 added an early return for '', but null takes a different path:
$str[0] evaluates to null and is handed straight to ord(). The other six
methods fail the same way with different messages, via strtoupper(),
strlen() in isMultibyte(), or preg_replace_callback().

Guard each entry point instead. Behaviour is unchanged -- every one of
these already returned '' for null -- but the caller now gets a single
MediaWiki deprecation naming the method, with a backtrace identifying the
call site. That is the piece T401193 has been missing: two reporters have
hit this and neither could be told where the null came from.

No caller in core passes null; the full unit and includes suites are clean
with the guards in place, which they would not be if one did.

Intended as the first half of a two-step change: once the deprecation has
been out for a release and callers are fixed, these parameters can be
declared `string` and the guards dropped.

new_description:
Add MwPageLookup shared component and the API composables

Alongside looking up users, features commonly need to provide a page
title lookup field. The API fetching and debouncing logic is the same
for both, so it now lives in reusable composables, in the new
resources/src/composables/ directory for sharing Vue.js composables
across MediaWiki features.

That work is split in two, because the two jobs have different users.
A survey of core and the extensions found the same three behaviours
written by hand in about 55 files: debounce what the user types, drop
a response that a newer one replaced, and stop a request that is on
its way. Six of those places stop every request of an API instance
that the caller gave them, not only their own, and two of the six are
in core. useMwRequest() owns that work for any component. The state of
a Codex Lookup is a smaller job with fewer users, so it stays apart in
useMwLookup().

Summary of changes:
* Add composables/common/useMwRequest.js. It gives a facade over an
API client that records the requests it starts, so that it stops
only those. The abort() of a client stops all of its requests, and
the caller can share the client with the rest of the application.
The composable also gives tokens, which tell a late response that a
newer one took its place; a debounce with the cancel() that
mw.util.debounce has not; and cleanup when the component goes away.
The caller gives the client, so the same code serves mw.Api, mw.Rest
and mw.ForeignApi.
* Add composables/common/useMwLookup.js, built on useMwRequest(). It
owns the menu item and search term state for a Codex Lookup.
Consumers provide a fetchResults() callback that maps API results to
menu items. An update for a value that is already on its way joins
that one, rather than stopping it and asking for the same results
again, which would leave the menu items empty for a caller that
waits. updateMenuItems() says what it did, so that such a caller can
tell "a newer update owns the menu items" from "the request failed".
clearMenuItems() drops the request for a prefix that the user
erased.
* Refactor MwUserLookup to make use of the new composables.
* Add components/common/MwPageLookup.vue, which fetches results from
list=prefixsearch and takes a 'namespace' prop.
* Add Jest tests for both composables and for MwPageLookup, and
include composables in Jest code coverage reporting.

old_description:
Add MwUserLookup shared component, make use of it in SpecialBlock

This kicks off the "Great Shared Vue Components Migration of 2026"™.
We start with MwUserLookup, refactored out of the battle-tested
UserLookup component of the mediawiki.special.block.codex module.

MwUserLookup features:
* Ability to use a custom API instance and options (though currently,
responses are expected to take the shape of the list=allusers API).
* Optional IP/range handling with CIDR limit validation. This logic was
moved from Special:Block, as it may serve useful in other applications
such as CheckUser and core Special:Contribs where CIDR limits apply.
* Validations are emitted through a 'validate' event that gives a
localized message, either from built-in validation or the native
validation message on the text input. This is proposed as a paradigm
for future shared components; Use native validation where possible,
and keep messages to a minimum, whilst providing Vue-powered
validations where it's deemed useful beyond a single use case.
* All CdxLookup props are accepted and passed through. This can be used
say to add the 'loadMore' functionality, which he shared component
deliberately leaves these out barring a shared need.

The shared components are Codex components themselves, so CodexModule
bundles them instead of a new module class. Modules request them with
the 'mwComponents' option, which adds the component files, their i18n
messages and their module dependencies, along with a synthetic
'mwComponents.js' file that exports them.

The components load Codex from resources/src/codex.js, a relative path
that CodexModule replaces with either the module's own Codex bundle or
the full '@wikimedia/codex' module. A module therefore does not have to
depend on all of Codex to use a shared component. When a module does
not otherwise use Codex, CodexModule tree-shakes in only the Codex
components that the shared components need.

The full set of shared components is also available as the
'mediawiki.components.common' module, for code that cannot use the
'mwComponents' option. That module tree-shakes: it bundles CdxLookup
alone, which is 66 KB of script and 21 KB of styles, in place of the
190 KB and 171 KB of the full library. The cost is a second copy of
CdxLookup on a page that also loads '@wikimedia/codex'.

For future patches:
* Move API and debouncing logic to a useMwApi() composable, for use in
other similar components such as MwPageLookup (T433558).
* Proper JSDoc generation and publishing at doc.wikimedia.org

[WIP] editPage.reauthPopup: Resubmit the form with requestSubmit()

Why:
- The reauth script stops the Save submit and later calls
form.submit(). That call does not fire submit handlers, so the
hCaptcha handler does not add its token. The POST also loses wpSave
- hCaptcha also stops the same submit and calls form.submit(). If
hCaptcha finishes first, the POST skips the reauth popup
- Users without skipcaptcha get "Incorrect or missing CAPTCHA" when
they save a reauth-gated page, for example MediaWiki:Common.css

What:
- Listen on the document in the capture phase and stop the first
Save submit before other handlers get it
- After the reauth check, resubmit with requestSubmit() and the
clicked button, so other submit handlers run and wpSave stays
- Keep form.submit() as a fallback when requestSubmit() is missing
- After a successful popup, check with the server on the next submit
instead of opening the popup again

old_description:
SchemaGenerator: Strip the extension root from symlinked extension paths

In the AbuseFilter extension, AbuseFilterSchemaTest fails when run
in a developer checkout where extensions are symlinked from the
extensions/ directory.

The reason is because when an extension is a symlink in
$wgExtensionDirectory to a clone elsewhere, normalizePath() resolves
the JSON path with realpath(), and the the resolved path is in neither
$wgExtensionDirectory nor MW_INSTALL_PATH, so no prefix is
stripped. Then generateSchemaSql.php and generateSchemaChangeSql.php
write the absolute path, including the developer's home directory,
into the "-- Source:" header, and tests based on
AbstractSchemaTestBase (e.g. AbuseFilterSchemaTest) fail against the
committed files. CI clones extensions directly into extensions/, so it
does not see this.

For a path outside $wgExtensionDirectory, go up to the nearest
directory with an extension.json or skin.json, and make the path
relative to it. This does not depend on how the extension was
installed. It also makes skins under core give "sql/foo.json" rather
than "skins/Name/sql/foo.json", as extensions do; no skin commits
generated SQL today. Core has no extension.json, so core's paths are
still relative to MW_INSTALL_PATH.

new_description:
Introduce HeaderSender utility for PHPUnit tests

Sending a header in PHPUnit tests is problematic because output has
already started, so PHP will emit a "headers already sent" warning. This
is currently worked around by having PHPUnit print to stderr and by
starting an output buffer early on in the PHPUnit bootstrap. However,
these complicate our PHPUnit configuration, and can interfere with other
tools, as explained in the task.

So, introduce a HeaderSender class that wraps the `header` function, and
effectively makes it a no-op in tests. Use it everywhere instead of
`header()`, except for WebStart which needs to call `header()` before
initializing MediaWiki. Also update some comments that show how to send
headers, while leaving some references to the `header()` function
untouched when the documentation doesn't really provide an example.

Provide a way to restore original header behaviour in tests if needed,
when actually testing headers. These tests will later need to use
PHPUnit process isolation.

If needed, this class could implement more complex behaviour such as
collecting headers in an array buffer that can be inspected in tests,
instead of just discarding them. However, that seems unnecessary for the
time being and is therefore not implemented here.

Four progress reporters read microtime() once and used the result both
as a timestamp, to render an ETA through wfTimestamp(), and as the
baseline for measuring elapsed time. Only the second is a duration.

new_description:
maintenance: Separate the timers from the clocks in dump progress

Four progress reporters read microtime() once and used the result both
as a timestamp, to render an ETA through wfTimestamp(), and as the
baseline for measuring elapsed time. Only the second is a duration.

TableCleanup and rebuildImages no longer keep a start timestamp at all.
Their ETA is now the current wall clock plus the time still to go,
rather than the start plus the estimated total. That is the same value,
because the start is the current time minus the elapsed time, and it is
steadier: the old form captured the clock once, so an adjustment
part way through skewed every later ETA, while a fresh reading
corrects itself.

The two dumpers still need a start timestamp, because their ETA has no
other epoch to build on, but everything else they measure now comes
from a timer. The per-report reading is not printed, so it is a timer
too, as are the previous report and the last checkpoint.

This is not only cosmetic. TextPassDumper decides when to roll a
checkpoint file from the gap between the last report and the last
checkpoint, so until now a clock adjustment could roll one early or
hold one back. That comparison is against maxTimeAllowed, which is in
seconds, so it converts the timer difference explicitly; without that
it would compare nanoseconds against seconds and roll a checkpoint
file on every report.

Names follow the distinction: a Time is a timestamp, a Timer is an
hrtime reading.

The two tests covering the checkpoint path are marked Broken and large
and do not run, so the comparison was checked directly instead: with a
limit of 0.5 seconds it stays false at 0.40 and turns true at 0.60,
and with 60 seconds it stays false at 59 and turns true at 61.

new_description:
tests: Make multi-slot tests parser agnostic, cover Parsoid MCR

RevisionRenderer::combineSlotOutput() combines the output of several
slots into one ParserOutput. It can combine at most one
Parsoid-rendered wikitext slot per revision. It throws an assertion
error if a second slot also holds Parsoid content.

Give the auxiliary slot JSON content, not wikitext content, in tests
that do not test wikitext-specific slot behavior (link extraction,
rendered text). JSON content is not Parsoid content, so it does not
hit the one-wikitext-slot limit. This makes
ApiQueryRecentChangesIntegrationTest::testSha1PropParameterWithMultipleSlots()
and ChangesListQueryTest parser agnostic: they now pass under both
the legacy parser and Parsoid, with no UseParsoidParser override.

Some tests still need the legacy parser:
* PageUpdaterTest's 'derivedslot' role has the wikitext content model
and many other tests in the same file share it, so these three
tests can not redefine it to JSON.
* DerivedPageDataUpdaterTest::testDoParserCacheUpdate() looks up
parser cache entries with ParserOptions that force the legacy
parser. Force the site default to match, so the cache entry under
test lands at the same cache key.
* ImportExportTest and PageDumpTestDataTrait's fixtures put wikitext
in more than one slot directly, and so hit the one-wikitext-slot
limit.

Add DerivedPageDataUpdaterTest::testPrepareContentParsoidMultiSlot(),
which exercises Parsoid's slot combination end to end. Parsoid stores
a non-main slot's HTML as an unhydrated ContentHolder fragment.
HydrateHeaderPlaceholders, part of the OutputTransform pipeline,
inserts a genuine slot-header element and the slot's HTML into the
final output. The new test saves a two-slot revision, then runs the
combined ParserOutput through the pipeline, and checks that both
slots' content and the slot header appear in the final HTML.

old_description:
Parsoid: Do not change ParserOptions in PageConfigFactory

PageConfigFactory::createFromParserOptions() changed the ParserOptions
of the caller. It set 'useParsoid', and it set the target language when
it got a page language override. The target language is not in the
cache key, so the change made isSafeToCache() return false. Thus
ParserCache and RevisionOutputCache did not save the output of a parse
that ran the selective update sample code.

Mutating the ParserOptions inside PageConfigFactory is a bad idea,
since this potentially makes the cache key used for storage (after
the parse) different from the cache key used for lookup (before the
parse). So let's remove the mutation:

* The callers that use a page language override (ParsoidHandler and
HtmlToContentTransform) now set the target language in their own
ParserOptions. ParsoidParser does not give a language to the
factory; the language it was passing is already available in the
ParserOutput if selective update should need it.
* Get the page language from the ParserOptions, in the same way as
Parser::getTargetLanguage().
* If 'useParsoid' is not set, emit a deprecation warning. Then clone the
ParserOptions and set 'useParsoid' on the clone. All callers in core now
set 'useParsoid' before they call the factory.
* Similarly, hard-deprecate the $pageLanguageOverride parameter. If provided,
clone the ParserOptions and set the target language on the clone.

maintenance/parse.php now sets 'useParsoid' where needed.
